data.title: Lupin Announces U.S. FDA Approval and Launch of Sitagliptin Tablets, USP in the United States
data.description:
Lupin Announces U.S. FDA Approval and Launch of Sitagliptin Tablets, USP in the United States

Lupin Announces U.S. FDA Approval and Launch of Sitagliptin Tablets, USP in the United States

PR Newswire

MUMBAI, India and NAPLES, Fla., Nov. 27, 2026

MUMBAI, India and NAPLES, Fla., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global pharmaceutical leader Lupin Limited (Lupin) (BSE: 500257) (NSE: LUPIN) (REUTERS: LUPIN.BO) (BLOOMBERG: LPCIN) today announced that following the approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) for its Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA), the company launched Sitagliptin Tablets USP, 25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg in the United States.

Sitagliptin Tablets USP, 25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg, are bioequivalent to the reference listed drug (RLD), Januvia® Tablets of Merck Sharp and Dohme LLC (Merck). Sitagliptin Tablets, USP are indicated for use as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Sitagliptin Tablets (RLD Januvia®) had estimated annual sales of USD 2,328.8 million in the U.S. (IQVIA MAT September 2026).

About Lupin

Lupin Limited is a global pharmaceutical leader headquartered in Mumbai, India, with a strong presence across India, the U.S., Other Developed Markets, and Emerging Markets, with products distributed in over 100 markets. Lupin has a diversified portfolio spanning generics, complex generics, specialty medicines, and biosimilars, and continues to strengthen its market position through a differentiated portfolio. The company maintains strong leadership in the U.S. and India across core therapeutic areas, including cardiovascular, respiratory, diabetes, gastrointestinal, and women's health. 15 state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities support sustainable operations, with 6 research centers and a dedicated workforce of over 26,000 professionals. Lupin continues to expand the healthcare ecosystem through diagnostics, digital health, patient-support programs, and disease management initiatives. Sustainability continues to be a core pillar of the company's business strategy.

To know more, visit www.lupin.com or follow us on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/lupin.

*Safe Harbor Statement 

Januvia is the registered trademark of Merck Sharp and Dohme LLC.

data.title: Canada Posts Budget Deficit in September on Public-Debt Charges — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada's budget deficit in September was largely unchanged from the same year-ago month, as a solid gain in personal-tax revenue was partly offset by hefty public-debt charges.

Canada's Department of Finance said the budget deficit in September stood at 5.14 billion Canadian dollars (US$3.61 billion), a slight rise from the year-ago C$5.02 billion shortfall. After the first six months of the current fiscal year, Ottawa is running a C$10.50 billion budget deficit, narrower compared with the C$16.09 billion from the same year-ago period.

The September data arrived weeks after the Liberal government's annual budget plan, which contemplates roughly C$140 billion in spending over the next half decade to fortify an economy struggling under the weight of U.S. tariffs. That spending is being partly financed by higher crude-oil prices, as Canada is a net exporter of the commodity.

The recent budget plan anticipates annual deficits of C$50 billion to C$60 billion, or under 2% of gross domestic product, over the next half-decade. The five-year forecast assumes average annual growth of just under 2%, and crude-oil prices averaging C$74 a barrel, or about 20% below current levels.

The public-finance data, available through the department's Fiscal Monitor publication, said total tax revenue in September rose 3.4% from a year ago. A 10% gain in personal-tax receipts was offset by a decline in sales-tax receipts, which officials attributed to the timing of assessments and refunds issued in the month.

Total expenses in September rose 5.1%. That was driven by a 10.4% increase in public-debt charges, due to higher average rates on an increased stock of bonds. Yields have climbed globally, reflecting expectations of higher inflation--fueled by elevated energy prices--and worries about sovereign debt levels.

The Canadian parliament's budget watchdog said in a report this month that a planned increase in nonbudgetary transactions contemplated by Prime Minister Mark Carney means the debt will grow about three times faster than the deficit over the next five years. This might leave federal finances exposed to unexpected rises in rates, the watchdog said.

data.title: A 66-year-old nurse is facing down retirement with just $500 saved. Who's to blame?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Retirement is a financial status, not an age'

"When you spend every dollar on lifestyle habits and car loans for decades instead of saving, you don't get to act surprised when the math doesn't work." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

Regarding the 66-year-old nurse (I'm 66, rely on Social Security and have just $500 in savings. What hope do I have?) having less than $500 to her name after a career in nursing isn't bad luck - it's the result of lifelong financial choices. Even putting aside $1,000-a-year over a few decades would have left her in a completely different position.

It's her fault. Retiring with zero savings isn't a viable plan, and there's no point in worrying about Social Security earnings limits when you don't have enough to live on. She didn't have a low-wage job; she had a solid career as a nurse, which makes the lack of a basic budget or safety net all the more frustrating.

When you spend every dollar on lifestyle habits and car loans for decades instead of saving, you don't get to act surprised when the math doesn't work. Retirement is a financial status, not an age - and without savings, she simply can't afford to stop working until 70. This is the problem with America. No one wants to be held accountable, even to themselves.

How many Starbucks did she have a week?

An Observer

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Don't miss: 'I experienced many years of poverty': I worked until 70. Why do wealthy retirees look down on those with less savings?

She could have been living paycheck-to-paycheck like millions of Americans or she could have, as you say in your letter, lost sight of the bigger picture.

Dear Observer,

Asking "why?" is often a fruitful question, if we keep an open mind.

We don't know how much that nurse was paid, and we don't know whether she was divorced or had difficulty paying rent. She could have lived paycheck-to-paycheck on stagnant wages and lost sight of the challenges that lie ahead. Most nurses work grueling 12-hour shifts. They don't retire out of entitlement; they retire because their knees and backs have given out.

Kindness is free, and it's often key to understanding what went right and wrong in people's lives, including our own. The average annual salary for nurses rose over the past 30 years from roughly $40,000 in the 2000s to $97,500 today, but those salaries depend on the medical facility, city/town and specialty. That income falls to $42,000 a year for nursing assistants and $64,400 for licensed vocational nurses.

I don't wish to change your view of her circumstances or why she is in the position she is in. Your views are your own. Yes, we all must take responsibility for our situation in life. We agree on that. But I prefer to frame her story as one of roads not taken and financial literacy, or lack thereof. She may also have had a catastrophic life event: divorce, a medical crisis or caring for an elderly relative.

Kindness is free and it's often key to understanding what went wrong.

This woman, for better or for worse, felt left out of the political discourse and conversations centering members of the middle class as a person who is living close to the poverty line. She collects $2,000 in Social Security, and also suggested that she is scared about what will happen when she is no longer able to work. She lives in a two-bedroom apartment with a roommate who is receiving disability benefits.

She may not be aware: When she reaches her full retirement age - 66 and 10 months or 67 years of age - there is no limit on how much she can earn without reducing how much she receives in Social Security benefits. Best of all, if any benefits were withheld earlier, the Social Security Administration will recalculate and increase her monthly check once she hits her FRA.

The nurse whose situation frustrates you is not unique. Multiple studies contend that just under half of retirees have less than $100,000 saved for retirement and, according to a 2025 report from the Transamerica Institute, 12% of retirees have no savings, and more than half (53%) rely on Social Security as their primary source of income throughout their retirement.

Don't miss: Spooked by Nvidia's turmoil? Play Grand Theft Auto VI instead of peeking at your 401(k).

Financial fragility

"Retirees face financial fragility, especially being vulnerable to economic uncertainty, inflation, rising healthcare costs, and financial market volatility - all factors that can easily erode their buying power on limited income," the report said. "Many are concerned about their health in older age and their ability to afford long-term care, yet many also have not solidified plans."

Achieving a secure retirement is, for some people, easier on paper. Lower-income workers who come up short in retirement often did not have a 401(k) at work, for instance, and research suggests that they tend to be women, who still experience a gender pay gap in part due to the kinds of jobs they have traditionally inhabited, as well as single adults and racial minorities.

Financial literacy has improved in recent decades. One study by researchers from Texas Tech University and the University of Michigan found that financial literacy declines steadily in older age, even though confidence in money-related decisions remains high. Average financial literacy scores increase up to 50 years of age and then begin to fall with age, they concluded.

Not everyone has the same start in life and chooses well-paid careers.

Access to education plays a role. Some 81% of college graduates versus 39% of adults with no college education have savings, and 68% of non-Hispanic white adults have a retirement savings plan versus 42% of people of color, Gallup found. Men (61%) are also more likely than women (57%) to have a retirement plan. (Women are more likely to be caretakers and homemakers.)

There's a lot, in fairness, that goes into making up the puzzle of any person's life story. Did I have an inheritance? What career did I choose? Was there a 401(k)? Did I suffer from an unexpected job loss, or a downturn in the market just as I was entering retirement? If we are honest, our journeys are a combination of upbringing, hard work, planning and dumb luck.

The 66-year-old's Social Security suggests she probably worked as hard as you or me. You learned either from your peers, parents or reading the financial press and, regardless of your profession, did not live above your means because you knew you had to put money aside for retirement and because you had the ability to do so. That's smart and savvy. But not everyone has the same start in life or chooses a well-paid career.

Some people have a margin of error to learn from their mistakes; others, alas, don't.

Related: Are you middle class? No, you're not. Here's why.

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

More columns from Quentin Fottrell:

'Poor people are not stupid': I grew up in poverty, earned $14 an hour, and inherited $150,000. Here's what I have learned from my windfall.

My father-in-law, 81, sold his $75,000 home to pay his daughter's $50,000 debt. How can I keep him from becoming destitute?

'Poverty doesn't have to be my reality': I thought I'd have to rely on Social Security. Then I taught myself how to invest.

-Quentin Fottrell

MDA SPACE COMPLETES ACQUISITION OF BLUE CANYON TECHNOLOGIES

MDA SPACE COMPLETES ACQUISITION OF BLUE CANYON TECHNOLOGIES

PR Newswire

TORONTO, Nov. 27, 2026

TORONTO, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MDA Space Ltd. (TSX: MDA) (NYSE: MDA) (the "Company"), a trusted mission partner to the rapidly expanding global defence and space industry, today announced that it has completed its previously announced acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies (BCT) LLC, a U.S.-based spacecraft and satellite component manufacturer and mission services provider, formerly part of RTX.

BCT brings 400 highly skilled employees in the Denver, Colorado space and aerospace hub, and more than 95 spacecraft launched and 4,300 products on orbit. Its addition to MDA Space provides the company with a strategic business and manufacturing footprint to capitalize on growing demand in the U.S. government market for defence space missions. With the close of the acquisition, BCT will be rebranded as MDA Space and operate as MDA Space USA. 

"I want to welcome the Blue Canyon Technologies team to MDA Space. The addition of BCT to MDA Space adds a strong and established business and team with domestic manufacturing capability that is ideally positioned to accelerate our growth strategy in the expanding U.S. defence market," said Mike Greenley, CEO of MDA Space. "Securing these strategic benefits on an accretive basis with a profitable and cash-generating business makes this an ideal fit for MDA Space global expansion and continued shareholder value creation."

Building the space between proven and possible, MDA Space (TSX:MDA) (NYSE:MDA) is a trusted mission partner to the global defence and space industry. A robotics, satellite systems and geointelligence pioneer with a 55-year+ story of world firsts and more than 450 missions, MDA Space is a global leader in communications satellites, Earth and space observation, and space exploration and infrastructure. The global MDA Space team of more than 4,000 space experts has the knowledge and know-how to turn an audacious customer vision into an achievable mission — bringing to bear a one-of-a-kind mix of experience, engineering excellence and wide-eyed wonder that's been in our DNA since day one. data.title: These stocks soared the most during a wild week highlighted by Huang's return to Nvidia
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Nvidia's stock soared this week, but was still down nearly 28% for November and 21% for 2026

The return of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as the company's CEO on Nov. 23 helped drive the entire U.S. stock market higher this week.

The broad U.S. stock indexes were all green early on Friday, as investors were closer to capping off a week of remarkable gains, sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO. Still, the gains only partially offset the previous week's declines.

The S&P 500 SPX was up 0.7% in early trading Friday, for a gain of 4.6% for the week as almost all of its components contributed. But that follows a decline of 8.6% the previous week through Friday, Nov. 20.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA was also up 0.7% early Friday, for a one-week gain of 4.9%, following a decline of 8% the previous week.

The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP) rose 0.8% early Friday and was up 5.1% for the week, following a 10% decline the previous week.

data.title: QFIN Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Qfin Holdings, Inc. Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
data.description:
QFIN Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Qfin Holdings, Inc. Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law

Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP (“SBS”), a national shareholder rights litigation firm, reminds investors of a class action lawsuit against Qfin Holdings, Inc. (“Qfin” or “the Company”) (NASDAQ: QFIN) for violations of §§10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Shareholders who purchased shares of QFIN during the class period listed are encouraged to contact the firm regarding possible lead plaintiff appointments. Appointment as lead plaintiff is not required to partake in any recovery.

CLASS PERIOD: March 18, 2026 to August 25, 2026

DEADLINE: November 27, 2026

If you are a shareholder who suffered a loss, click here to participate.

CASE DETAILS: According to the Complaint, the Company made false and misleading statements to the market. Qfin misled investors over its ability to deliver strong financial results in the face of regulatory changes. The Company downplayed the negative impacts of regulatory headwinds. Based on these facts, the Company’s public statements were false and materially misleading throughout the class period. When the market learned the truth about Qfin, investors suffered damages.

We also encourage you to contact Brian Schall or David Schwartz of Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP, 2049 Century Park East, Suite 2460, Los Angeles, CA 90067, at 310-301-3335, to discuss your rights free of charge. You can also reach us through the firm's website at www.schallfirm.com, or by email at david@schallfirm.com.

The class, in this case, has not yet been certified, and until certification occurs, you are not represented by an attorney. If you choose to take no action, you can remain an absent class member.

Join the case to recover your losses

WHY SBS? Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP represents investors around the world and specializes in securities class action lawsuits and shareholder rights litigation. Bringing together the extensive experience and diverse skillsets of founding partners Brian Schall, Andrew Brown, and David Schwartz, SBS is dedicated to aggressively advocating for every investor.

This press release may be considered Attorney Advertising in some jurisdictions under the applicable law and rules of ethics.
